thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate and DNS resolution variance for PrivateLink endpoints in us-central1. Automatic grouping: DNS TTL surge + AZ-forwarding mismatches. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Seeing spike in 5xxs + client reconnects. Any customer-visible reports?

kevin.l: Getting a DM from SEs — one enterprise customer reports intermittent 502s when calls route to AZ-B. They say some sessions drop and retry ends up in the wrong AZ.

sarah.m: I can see a pattern in the logs: the PrivateLink frontends return two different private IPs across DNS queries, TTLs are 1s->120s in bursts. That will cause clients to cache wrong targets mid-session.

jordan.r: netops, can you confirm if there were any recent route reflector changes or peering churn? BGP metrics look noisy around the same time window.

netops: We rolled an update to RR set in us-central1 about 12:20 UTC — intended to add a new passive reflector for load spread. Noted several ephemeral BGP withdraws seconds after that. We're checking config diffs now.

eng-runtime: On our side, the serving runtime logged lots of L7 connection resets to one AZ IP. KV cache hits dropped on those nodes. Suspect a DNS -> routing mismatch.

oncall-sre: Ok plan: 1) Fail-open affected customers to public endpoints where possible. 2) Force DNS flush on PrivateLink resolvers and pin TTL temporarily to 30s. 3) If BGP noise persists, revert RR change. 4) Keep customer comms updated. Who can exec 1?

kevin.l: I'll coordinate fail-open with Customer Success and apply the routing override for the specific customer tenant pool. Doing a dry-run now.

ops-lead: @kevin.l please add a flag so traffic can be reverted quickly. Also, notify cloud provider support that our RR update correlated with peering withdraws.

netops: Provider case opened. They acknowledge seeing route churn at the MM-IX level and say they're investigating. Meanwhile I'm preparing to rollback the RR update — need a thumbs from eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: Thumbs. Revert the RR update. Also, I'll push a temporary circuit-breaker: if an endpoint sees >5 resets in 30s, we mark it unhealthy and remove from pool. That will reduce client flapping.

oncall-sre: Executing steps: 1) applied customer-specific fail-open at 12:52 UTC -> traffic drained to public endpoint. 2) flushed PrivateLink resolvers via `dig +trace` helper and reloaded dnsmasq on resolvers. Command used:```bash
sudo systemctl restart dnsmasq
for ip in $(cat /etc/privatelink-resolvers); do dig @${ip} +short privatelink.acme.internal; done
```

sarah.m: After flush, TTL stabilized around 30s. We're temporarily setting TTL override via resolver policy until upstream issue fixed. Also increasing health-check frequency for affected endpoints from 10s to 5s.

jordan.r: Rolling back RR update at 12:56 UTC. BGP withdraw spikes have stopped on our peers. We will keep monitoring for 15m.

netops: Confirmed — after rollback, route churn tailing off. Provider says their MM-IX fabric had an internal flap but our RR change coincided with a vulnerable window. Case ID: CLOUD-23712 (provider).

eng-runtime: Circuit-breaker engaged. We're seeing error rates drop from 12% -> 2% for the affected customer. KV cache warmup is ongoing for the nodes that were marked unhealthy and then re-added.

kevin.l: Customer notified at 13:05 UTC: we described the mitigation and temporary fail-open to public endpoints. CS to follow up on client-side DNS caches and recommend application backoff. They acknowledged.

ops-lead: Next steps: 1) Keep TTL override for 60m then step down to 120s. 2) Provider to share root cause. 3) Postmortem if degradation >30m or customer SLA breach. 4) Follow-up RFC on RR rollout gating for PrivateLink paths.

oncall-sre: Logging timeline to incident tracker. Adding comms to Status page draft. If anyone sees regression, ping +1.

incident-bot: NOTE: Handoff to next oncall in 45m. Current severity: Sev2 -> under active mitigation.

sarah.m: Quick snippet of the health-check filter we used:```json
{"health_check": {"interval": 5, "failure_threshold": 3, "success_threshold": 2}}
```

jordan.r: Reverting TTL override at 13:42 UTC as route stability confirmed for 30m. Gradually returning traffic back to PrivateLink; watching for asymmetric hits.

eng-runtime: Final metrics: 5xxs back to baseline, DNS variance gone. We'll keep increased health-checks for 2h and then normalise.

ops-lead: Great job everyone. We'll capture blocker in postmortem and draft RR rollout checklist change.

kevin.l: Closing customer loop: CS will run a sync with their network team to clear client caches; ops to confirm after their flush.

oncall-sre: Marking thread for postmortem. Logging timestamps and commands used. Leaving oncall watch until Handoff.

incident-bot: RESOLVED (mitigated): DNS TTL surge + RR change correlation; rollback + fail-open + resolver flush mitigated customer impact.
